proposal.blind_spot: All kernels look identically DRAM-bound, so the optimizer cannot tell roofline-bound kernels (rewrites must regress) from L1TEX-transaction-bound ones (vectorization wins), and cannot see whether the dominant write traffic wastes sectors.

rationale.l1tex__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustai: HIGH -> bottleneck is L1TEX transaction throughput, not DRAM bytes; issue fewer/wider accesses via 128-bit vectorized loads/stores and larger contiguous per-thread tiles / LOW with high dram% -> already at DRAM roofline; do not restructure accesses, only pursue byte-reducing fusion or leave the kernel unchanged
rationale.smsp__sass_average_data_bytes_per_sector: HIGH -> stores already fully coalesced; leave store side alone and focus elsewhere or accept roofline / LOW -> writes waste sectors (masked or strided stores, common here since writes equal or exceed reads); fix store indexing for full 32-byte sectors and contiguous aligned output tiles
